title: ACCRINT: one identification lattice, two fresh gates, thirteen open rows

upstream_anchor.section: Lane B — LANDED + TWICE-HELD-OUT GATED (2026-07-20, agent-W)

status_plain: ACCRINT is held-out gated and still open at the same time, and both are true. The identification lattice b39 scored 25,407 of 25,410; two fresh corpora, b40 and b42, scored 51,417 of 51,420 and 68,783 of 68,790; the source calls the discipline TWICE-HELD-OUT GATED and uses the word fresh for both. The combined figure the source also publishes, 145,607 of 145,620, is a MIXED corpus: it contains the identification lattice the repair was fitted against. It may never be described as held out. Each component is recorded here as its own count so a page can render the fresh gates without laundering the lattice through them. The row is still open: thirteen bistable rows survive, all at rate 0.0615, and the source says they are not accepted.

evidence_locality_note: Batteries b39, b40, b42 and b43 and the agent record `smart-fuzzer/work/w109/...` live under gitignored `smart-fuzzer/` subtrees; no artifact is tracked at commit 473efa3.
substrate: calc_method=FALSE is a flat fraction with a whole-period skip; calc_method=TRUE is a period walk summed BACKWARD from settlement to issue, with an act/act issue stub by its own length and a settlement-side period that is always fractional even on coupon dates. All plain SSE2 f64: ACCRINT sits in the 2010-rewrite SSE2 body class with GRATIO and BRATIO, not the x87 legacy-financial class.
ruled_out: x87 emulation for either path: "x87 emulation strictly worse on both paths"
the forward period walk for calc_method=TRUE: it is 1 ULP off on about 9 per cent of rows
